cards.front: What should you know about spectators?
cards.back: People who watch sporting events, either at the venue in person or through media coverage. Spectators are a vital part of the sporting experience, providing atmosphere, revenue and motivation for performers.

cards.front: What should you know about hooliganism?
cards.back: Disorderly, aggressive and violent behaviour by spectators at sporting events, most commonly associated with football. Hooliganism involves organised groups of fans who engage in fighting, vandalism and intimidation, often planning confrontations in advance.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — spectator behaviour and hooliganism?
cards.back: 1. For Spectator Behaviour and Hooliganism questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Spectator Behaviour and Hooliganism to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

Separate areas, entrances and exits for rival fans (e.g. Very effective - reduces direct contact)
Legal orders preventing attendance at matches (e.g. Effective - removes known troublemakers)
No alcohol in view of pitch; limited sales (e.g. Moderately effective - reduces aggression)
High-risk matches start earlier (e.g. Moderately effective - less drinking time)
Every spectator has an allocated seat (e.g. Very effective - improved control and safety)

Students often say alcohol is banned at football. Wrong: "Alcohol is banned at all football matches." Correct: "Alcohol cannot be consumed in view of the pitch at English football league matches, but it can be consumed in concourse areas. The restriction applies to the seating/playing area, not the entire venue."
